references.text: Moses also describes the Lord's coming from Seir and his revelation from Mount Paran, using similar theophanic imagery.
David uses almost identical language to describe God's march through the wilderness, where the earth shook and the heavens poured down rain at God's presence.
Habakkuk describes God's coming from Teman and Mount Paran with similar cosmic signs and earthquakes.
The psalmist describes how the waters saw God and trembled, while the clouds poured out water—a similar theophany.
At Mount Sinai, the entire mountain shook violently when the Lord descended, a foundational account of a theophany.
Isaiah asks who comes from Edom and Bozrah, linking the Lord's revelation to the region of Edom.
